correctness.rationale: The eight basis vectors and seven structure constants define the free two-generated class-four Lie algebra. Its center is exactly the three-dimensional top homogeneous component. Reducing an arbitrary almost-inner derivation modulo the center leads to a five-dimensional free class-three quotient whose almost-inner derivations are directly proved inner over every field. After inner subtraction a central map has four parameters (p,h,r,s); the exact determinant criterion is alpha*beta*(alpha*(s-h)+beta*(p-r))=0 for all alpha,beta. Over the two-element field it is one linear relation; over any larger field it forces p=r and h=s. Central inner maps form precisely the latter two-dimensional subspace. Hence dim(AID/Inn)=1 over F2 and 0 otherwise; dim Inn=5. Stand-alone verify.py checked Jacobi, derivation, field sizes 2,3,4, and every algebra element over F2, ending VERIFY_OK. The finite program is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Almost-inner quotients are a natural local-global invariant of Lie algebras. For a canonical free class-four algebra the theorem identifies the first two-generator nilpotency class in which F2 acquires an outer almost-inner derivation, proves a sharp field-cardinality dichotomy F2 versus F4 despite equal characteristic, and gives an explicit map, exact quotient dimension and labeled finite-field counts. This is a substantive boundary to a literature theorem whose infinite-field hypothesis is essential, not a routine arbitrary parameter calculation.
